stem: A nurse reviews routine kidney screening for an adult with type 2 diabetes who has no known chronic kidney disease. Which tests should the nurse expect to be assessed at least annually?

options.A: A random urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)
options.B: A urine dipstick for glucose and an annual chest radiograph
options.C: A serum glucose level alone because dedicated kidney tests are unnecessary until symptoms develop
options.D: A 24-hour urine collection alone without assessment of glomerular filtration

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend at least annual assessment of kidney function with a random UACR and eGFR in all people with type 2 diabetes. Both measures are important because diabetic CKD can present with albuminuria, reduced eGFR, or both, and reduced eGFR without albuminuria occurs in diabetes. B and C do not provide the recommended CKD screening. D is incomplete and unnecessarily substitutes a burdensome timed collection for the preferred spot UACR while omitting eGFR.
educational_objective: Screen adults with type 2 diabetes for chronic kidney disease using both spot UACR and eGFR at least annually rather than relying on urine albumin or blood glucose alone.
source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
source_document_title: Chronic Kidney Disease and Risk Management: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_locator: Recommendation 11.1a — assess kidney function with random UACR and eGFR at least annually in all people with type 2 diabetes; ‘Assessment of Albuminuria and Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate’ — spot UACR preferred over timed collections; ‘Diagnosis of CKD’ — CKD may present with albuminuria and/or reduced eGFR
source_claim_supported: Current ADA screening for diabetic CKD requires both random UACR and eGFR at least annually in type 2 diabetes; urine albumin testing alone is not sufficient to capture all CKD presentations.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential; monitor and interpret diagnostic studies used to detect complications of chronic disease
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — CKD screening in diabetes using UACR and eGFR
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item because it overemphasized ‘urine microalbumin’ as the primary screening method. ADA 2026 requires both UACR and eGFR, uses modern UACR terminology, and notes that CKD can occur with reduced eGFR without albuminuria. The item was reclassified from Physiological Adaptation to Reduction of Risk Potential because it tests screening/diagnostic monitoring.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified directly against ADA Standards of Care 2026 Section 11. The current recommendation explicitly pairs random UACR with eGFR for annual screening in type 2 diabetes.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A reproduces the exact screening tests and population. The rationale avoids labeling a single abnormal result as definitive CKD and does not add unsupported diagnostic thresholds to the question.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; both UACR and eGFR are recommended.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; these are not the recommended CKD screening tests.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; CKD screening is recommended before symptoms and requires kidney-specific testing.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; spot UACR is preferred in most screening contexts and eGFR is also required.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A includes both recommended kidney measures without substituting a less appropriate test.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are plausible laboratory/screening strategies rather than unrelated diagnoses.
audit_findings.blueprint: Reduction of Risk Potential is the best fit because the nurse is recognizing appropriate diagnostic surveillance for a chronic complication.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked type 1 versus type 2 timing, UACR versus ‘microalbumin’ terminology, eGFR-without-albuminuria phenotype, spot versus 24-hour collection, category mapping, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
